summary: Azure Application Gateway health-probe teardown intermittently suppresses SSE terminal event causing client hang
description: Customer reports that long-running server-sent events (SSE) streams occasionally never receive the final 'event: done' terminal message after an intermediate TCP/HTTP teardown initiated by an Azure Application Gateway health probe. Client remains connected via a reconnect flow but the final terminal event is not emitted and the client stalls waiting for completion. This appears to only affect streams that were near completion when the probe-induced teardown occurred.
impact: A subset of NovaDocs users see generated responses that never signal completion; UX shows an indefinite 'generating...' state. No extra tokens billed in most observed cases but customer workflow times out and triggers retries, increasing downstream API traffic. Approximately 7% of long-tail streaming sessions affected for this customer in last 48h.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer opens SSE stream against /v1/streams with a prompt that yields a final short completion (~3-8 tokens).
2) Azure Application Gateway health probe configured with aggressive idle timeout runs during last 1-2 seconds of the stream.
3) Probe triggers connection teardown and the client performs reconnect/Resume with X-Stream-Resume header containing last-received-offset.
4) Client receives partial final tokens but never receives terminal 'event: done' or 'event: error'.
5) Client waits until its own timeout or issues duplicate request.
observed_behavior: Partial final tokens delivered, sometimes a duplicate trailing token sequence on a later reconnect, and no terminal 'done' event. Client logs show successful resume ACK but UI never transitions to finished. Server logs show request handler marked as completed in some backends but final end-frame not routed to the reconnecting connection.
expected_behavior: After reconnect/resume the client should receive a full ordered stream including a single terminal 'event: done' so the client can finalize the response and stop retries.
logs:
[2026-03-12T15:02:11Z] proxy: conn 0x7f3a closed by appgw probe
[2026-03-12T15:02:11Z] srv: stream handler completed id=abc123 backend=sr-42 but terminal-frame not flushed to conn 0x7f3b
[2026-03-12T15:02:11Z] client: resume sent X-Stream-Resume:offset=1454
[2026-03-12T15:02:12Z] client: received data: "data: \"...final token\"\n\n"
[2026-03-12T15:02:34Z] client: waiting for 'event: done' (timeout 30s)
investigation_notes:
- Reproduced in lab with AGW configured to probe idle connections: saw identical symptom when probe fired within 0.5-1.5s of completion.
- Backend logs show handler believes it emitted end-marker, but the end marker is not present on the connection that the client reconnects to.
- Likely race between AGW connection termination, backend worker completing the stream, and the reconnect path selecting a different worker without the final event.
- Hypothesis: connection-affinity loss combined with our resume token mapping logic can cause the final frame to be dropped when the origin completes during the probe window.
- No evidence of tokenization/ordering corruption; issue is missing terminal event routing only.
temporary_workarounds:
1) Increase AGW idle probe interval / disable aggressive probe for affected endpoint.
2) Client-side: treat receipt of trailing tokens + N seconds with no terminal event as implicit completion (not ideal).
3) For customers on Dedicated, pin connection affinity to reduce cross-worker handoff.
root_cause_summary: Race between Azure Application Gateway health-probe-induced TCP teardown and the server-side stream finalization which leads to terminal 'done' event not being routed to the reconnecting client. Resume logic assumes final event either already reached client or will be retransmitted from same worker, but AGW teardown may cause reconnect to be serviced by a different worker lacking that final frame.
mitigation_plan:
Short term: doc workaround to adjust AGW probe configuration and advise client resilience patterns. Medium term: implement idempotent terminal-event replay in resume flow so a worker that detects a completed stream can supply terminal frame to a reconnecting client even if a different worker owns the reconnect. Also evaluate path to use cluster-level final-frame replication or central resume-ack broker.
Timeline: prototype within 2 sprints; hotfix mitigation (tighter resume checks) targeted this week on canary.
final_resolution: (pending) Prototype of server-side terminal-frame replay has been implemented in feature branch and is under canary. Customer agreed to apply AGW probe config changes this morning; monitoring shows no further hangs for amended sessions. Final rollout scheduled after validation. Will update when PR merged and deployed across prod.
workaround_provided_to_customer: Yes - advised to tune AGW probe/idle timeout and recommended client fallback heuristics. Support provided sample AGW config and connectivity tests.
next_steps:
1) Run canary of terminal-frame replay change in us-west with NovaDocs traffic.
2) Collect telemetry for 72h and validate no missing terminal events.
3) If validated, schedule global rollout and postmortem.
4) Update streaming runbook with proxy probe guidance.
